title: The Future of Jobs Report 2025 - Skills outlook
author: World Economic Forum
annotation: The employer survey anticipates changing skill needs through 2030 and emphasizes analytical, technical, creative, and adaptive capabilities. I use it to justify a mixed competency map, while treating employer expectations as forecasts rather than guaranteed outcomes.

title: Anthropic Economic Index: AI's impact on software development
author: Anthropic
annotation: This analysis examines 500,000 coding interactions and distinguishes task automation from collaboration with developers. It helps me examine how implementation work could change, but it does not measure final code quality or prove productivity gains.

title: GDC 2026 State of the Game Industry Reveals Impact of Layoffs, Generative AI, and More
author: Beth Elderkin
annotation: The official survey summary describes AI use, employment pressures, and contrasting attitudes among game-industry professionals. I use it to challenge the assumption that easier production automatically means easier entry into games, while recognizing that respondents do not represent every studio.

title: Applied AI Demo Engineer
author: Anthropic
annotation: This employer listing combines LLM applications, retrieval, integrations, reliable prototypes, and technical communication. I use its duties as one concrete role comparison rather than an entry-level promise or a universal definition of AI engineering.

title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
author: Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab
annotation: MIT CSAIL researchers report early experiments in which a language model directly reads, writes, or edits another neural network's weights. I am studying this work as a possible direction for AI engineering, while treating its experimental results as an invitation to investigate rather than proof of general reliability.

title: Replicating Weight-Space Programming: Writing and Reading Neural Network Weights with Frontier LLMs
author: Roksana Goworek, Alexander Hickey, Federico Nanni, and Martin O'Reilly
annotation: The Alan Turing Institute reproduces some weight-reading and weight-writing results while identifying limits in generalization and interpretation. I use this comparison to frame my interest around reproducible experiments and evaluation rather than assume that the original demonstrations establish broad model understanding.
